not duplicated here.

specs.title: User Stories (Cases)
specs.summary: The verbose, story-level source of truth (UC-1..UC-40) — the Use-Case Index, per-role UX notes, the ~35-event notification/alert schema, media-delivery specs by space type, and representative end-to-end journeys. Specs win when a story and a spec disagree.
specs.body:
> The verbose, story-level source of truth for what each role does. The canonical DESIGN
> (modules, enums, policies) is in §1–18 — when a story and a spec ever disagree, the spec wins.
> All `[owner YYYY-MM-DD]` decisions are folded in. This is intentionally the longest section.

Scenario prose for each role is folded into §1–14 specs and the journeys below; only the
non-redundant UX details unique to stories are kept here.
Every user story / case / journey carries a stable **UC-N** code (backend functions/classes tag the
UC they satisfy — e.g. `design.json UC-7`; the full index is
`userStories[]`). `UC-N — title — primary spec §`:

<!-- [owner 2026-07-29] Promoted two suggested proposals to canonical UCs: F01→UC-41 (actor USER, since every role is a type of user; ACCOUNTS stays reserved for multi-user accounts) and §11→UC-42 (actor CLIENT). UC-42 is framed around user SUCCESS with the unified chat UX, not the tickets→chat merge history. The remaining infra/meta proposals (§0,§1,§15–§20,DASH-1) stay 'suggested' — their actors are docs readers / engineers, not platform users, so they are not user stories. -->
USER (cross-cutting — every role is a type of user)
- UC-41 — User signs in and the platform grants exactly their role's capabilities (RBAC-scoped workspace; failed login is clear & non-leaky) — §1, §14
- UC-43 — Every screen and endpoint authorizes by the OWNERSHIP CHAIN (user → account → campaign → adset → ad; space → provider account). A break anywhere returns 404, never 403. Cross-account moves are refused; same-account moves carry their bookings. — §21, §14

CLIENT
- UC-1 — Client searches & multi-selects spaces on the map — §5
- UC-2 — Client organizes campaign / adset / ads from the backlog — §4, §5
- UC-3 — Client uploads spec-validated creative — §4, §5
- UC-4 — Client checks out & pays (ONE invoice per campaign) — §8
- UC-5 — Client books-for-later / pre-pays into escrow (AFTER-MVP) — §6
- UC-6 — Client reviews & ACCEPTS proof → payout releasable — §7
- UC-7 — Client REJECTS proof / flags mismatch → dispute (3 chats + hold) — §7, §10
- UC-8 — Client opens a provider inquiry FROM the provider's published space/ad listing (space attached; the ONLY path to a provider — providers have no public profile/UI) — §10
- UC-9 — Client contacts Support from Messages or an ad/adset/campaign object (object = context, provider NOT pulled in); a Billing-opened chat is Support-fronted with the payment attached (Payments looped in via the internal chat) — §10
- UC-10 — Client cancels a booking (refund per policy) — §8
- UC-11 — Client views wallet & withdraws — §8
- UC-12 — Client rates a provider (AFTER-MVP) — §9
- UC-42 — User resolves everything in one seamless conversation — no juggling tickets vs chat (one uniform chat UI; Support, and Payments when money is involved, join the same thread) — §10, §11

PROVIDER
- UC-13 — Provider lists a space & declares specs — §4, §5
- UC-14 — Provider manages availability calendar (iCal sync) — §13
- UC-15 — Provider approves / rejects a booking request — §5
- UC-16 — Provider / Installator uploads the PRIMARY proof — §7
- UC-17 — Provider receives a payout — §8
- UC-18 — Provider views strike counter / appeals a strike — §7

ACCOUNTS & COLLABORATORS
- UC-19 — Owner invites & manages collaborators — §3, §14
- UC-20 — Collaborator acts within subrole scope — §3

SUPPORT
- UC-21 — Support joins a client↔provider chat (announced, PII relax) — §10
- UC-22 — Support investigates a dispute & RAISES a money flag — §7, §10
- UC-23 — Support edits a non-money object (audited) — §12
- UC-24 — Support reverses a strike (audited) — §7

PAYMENTS
- UC-25 — Payments approves/executes payment & payout (processing queue) — §8
- UC-26 — Payments executes a refund — §8
- UC-27 — Payments huddles with Support in the internal chat — §10

ADMIN
- UC-28 — Admin chat oversight (read-only, incognito) — §10, §12
- UC-29 — Admin moderation: takedown / restore / freeze — §12
- UC-30 — Admin configures System Configurations + RBAC matrix — §12, §14
- UC-31 — Admin reviews the immutable audit log — §12
- UC-32 — Admin payout-stop window & clawback decision — §8

END-TO-END JOURNEYS (composite — see below)
- UC-33 — Journey: first-time client, single billboard (UC-1..4, UC-6) — §19
- UC-34 — Journey: first-time provider (UC-13..17) — §19
- UC-35 — Journey: disputed proof (UC-7, UC-22, UC-25, UC-27) — §7, §10
- UC-36 — Journey: ad creative & installation actor boundaries — §5, §7
- UC-37 — Admin deletion guardrails / "programmed for deletion" (no hard-delete with open chat / active booking / unsettled funds) — §12
- UC-38 — Notifications & alert-schema dispatch (domain events → channel/urgency fan-out) — §13
- UC-39 — Provider self-pause / unpublish a space (reversible; no new bookings while paused) — §12
- UC-40 — Proof-deadline cron: day-3/4 reminders → day-5 auto-cancel + full refund + strike — §7
<!-- [owner 2026-07-17] UC-37..40 added from the design audit; their specs live in §12/§13/§7. "Dispute opened" is an ALERT emitted by UC-7's auto-open to Support/Payments, not a separate manual action. -->


= CLIENT UX notes (not already in specs) =  (UC-1, UC-2, UC-3, UC-4)
- Multi-select spaces → "Add to a new/existing campaign" + a 10-second "Go to my new campaign"
  toast; selected spaces sit in the backlog until placed in an adset.
- "Send all selected to a new adset"; the campaign view's Orphan-spaces list has a one-click
  "Move all to new adset"; orphans can't reach checkout.
- The upload control shows the provider's upload-instructions summary inline, kept visible
  during/after upload; on spec-mismatch the upload is rejected with a clear message (e.g. "your
  file must be PDF/X-1a, CMYK, 150 DPI at trim, 1 cm bleed").
- Refund policy, terms & conditions, and privacy policy are linked in the footer and on the
  checkout screen before paying.

= PROVIDER UX notes =  (UC-13, UC-14, UC-15, UC-16, UC-17, UC-18)
- Media specs auto-populate from a per-type template (provider can tighten) plus free-text rules.
- Confirmed bookings move to an installation queue (install date + client file), viewable by
  Installator collaborators.
- Revenue dashboard: upcoming / held / paid / refunded + trailing-90-day strike counter.

(SUPPORT / PAYMENTS / ADMIN story details are fully covered by §2 powers, §7 proof/strikes,
§8 money, §10 chats, §12 admin — UC-21..UC-32; not restated here.)

= NOTIFICATION & ALERT SCHEMA =
Columns: Event | Trigger | Recipients (roles) | Channel | Urgency | Message template (≤140).

| Event | Trigger | Recipients | Channel | Urgency | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New booking request | Client checkout completes | Provider | in-app+email | high | "New booking on {space}: {dates}, {total} MXN. Approve/reject within 48h." |
| Booking approved | Provider approves | Client(+collabs), Support(log) | in-app+email | med | "Your booking on {space} is approved. Display starts {date}." |
| Booking rejected | Provider rejects | Client(+collabs) | in-app+email | high | "Booking on {space} rejected: {reason}. Funds returned to wallet." |
| Booking confirmed (provider picks) | Provider approves one from the queue (chooses which offer wins) | Client, Provider | in-app+email | med | "Booking for {space} on {dates} confirmed. Display begins {date}." |
| Day-3 proof reminder | Display +3d, no proof | Provider | in-app+email | med | "Upload proof for {ad} in 2 days or it auto-cancels." |
| Day-4 proof reminder | Display +4d, no proof | Provider | in-app+email+SMS | high | "Last day to upload proof for {ad}. Tomorrow it auto-cancels + strike." |
| Proof uploaded | Provider uploads | Client(+collabs) | in-app+email | low | "Proof uploaded for {ad}. Review under Campaigns." |
| Proof accepted | CLIENT accepts (not Payments) | Client, Provider, Payments | in-app+email | low | "Proof accepted for {ad}. Payment now releasable." |
| Proof rejected | CLIENT rejects / collab flags | Provider, Client, Support+Payments (3 chats, payout held) | in-app+email | high | "Proof on {ad} rejected: {reason}. Payment held; Payments+Support will review the case." |
| Secondary mismatch flagged | Client/collab flags | Provider, Payments, Support | in-app+email | high | "Mismatch flag on {ad}. Payout held pending review." |
| Cancel by client pre-approval | Client cancels before approval | Provider | in-app+email | low | "Booking on {space} cancelled before approval. No charge." |
| Cancel by client post-approval | Client cancels after approval, pre-display | Provider, Payments, Support | in-app+email | high | "Booking on {space} cancelled. Refund per policy." |
| Cancel by provider after confirm | Provider cancels confirmed booking | Client, Payments, Support, Admin | in-app+email+SMS | critical | "{space} booking cancelled by provider. Full refund to wallet." |
| Auto-cancel on proof miss | Day-5 elapsed, no proof | Client, Provider, Payments, Support | in-app+email | critical | "{ad} auto-cancelled — no proof. Full refund. Strike on provider." |
| Refund issued | Refund executed | Client, Support | in-app+email | high | "{amount} MXN refunded to your wallet for {ad}. Withdrawable now." |
| Refund failed | Gateway error | Payments, Support, Admin | in-app+email+SMS | critical | "Refund for {ad} failed at {gateway}. Manual intervention required." |
| Dispute opened | Client opens dispute | Support, Provider | in-app+email | high | "Dispute opened on {ad}. Support reviews within 24h." |
| Dispute resolved valid | Support sides with client | Client, Provider, Payments | in-app+email | high | "Dispute on {ad} resolved for client. Refund processing." |
| Dispute resolved invalid | Support sides with provider | Client, Provider | in-app+email | med | "Dispute on {ad} closed. Provider payout proceeds." |
| Payout held | Mismatch flag / open dispute | Provider, Payments | in-app+email | high | "Payout for {ad} held pending review." |
| Payout released | Proof accepted, no holds | Provider | in-app+email | low | "Payout of {amount} MXN released for {ad}." |
| Strike accrued | Missed proof / provider cancel / upheld mismatch | Provider, Support | in-app+email | high | "Strike accrued: {reason}. {n}/3 in 90 days." |
| 3-strike admin alert | 3 strikes in 90 days | Support, Admin | in-app+email | critical | "Provider {name} hit 3 strikes. Review for freeze." |
| Support joined chat | Support enters chat | Client, Provider | in-app | low | "Support joined this chat. PII masking relaxed." |
| PII attempted | Pattern match phone/email/URL | Sender | in-app | low | "We masked your message — sharing contact info isn't allowed before Support joins." |
| Collaborator invited | Client adds collaborator email | Invited collaborator | email | low | "You've been invited to collaborate on {account}. Accept to view its campaigns and proofs." |
| Listing taken down | Admin moderates | Provider | in-app+email | high | "Your listing {space} was taken down: {reason}." |
| Listing restored | Admin restores | Provider | in-app+email | low | "Your listing {space} is live again." |
| Provider frozen | Admin freezes | Provider, Payments | in-app+email | critical | "Your provider account is frozen. New bookings paused, upcoming cancelled (clients refunded)." |
| Ad rejected by provider | Provider rejects a file | Client(+collabs) | in-app+email | high | "Your ad on {space} was rejected: {reason}. No charge. Re-upload a corrected file." |
| Pre-pay offer placed | Client pre-pays a slot | Provider, Client | in-app+email | low | "Pre-pay offer on {space} for {dates}. {total} MXN in escrow." |
| Pre-pay offer expired | Slot didn't open in window | Client | in-app+email | med | "Pre-pay offer on {space} expired. {amount} MXN returned to wallet." |
| Calendar setup stale | Calendar older than threshold (7d) | Provider | in-app | low | "Calendar for {space} is {n} days old. Refresh it or connect a live URL." |
| Collaborator opened a chat | Collaborator opens a support chat | Client(owner), Support | in-app+email | med | "{collaborator} opened a support chat on {campaign}." |
| Mismatch flag filed (ack) | Client/collab flags mismatch | Flagger | in-app | low | "Your mismatch flag on {ad} was filed. Payout held; Support will review." |

= MEDIA-DELIVERY SPECS BY SPACE TYPE =
Columns: Space type | Provider declares (physical) | Client must deliver (file).

| Space type | Provider declares (physical) | Client must deliver (file) |
|---|---|---|
| Billboard (printed) | W×H cm; substrate (vinyl/paper/mesh); viewing distance; install method | PDF/X-1a or TIFF; CMYK; 150 DPI at trim¹; 1 cm bleed; outlined fonts; ≤200 MB |
| Digital screen (big, outdoor) | Pixel res (e.g. 1920×1080); orientation; loop slot length (s); brightness (nits); refresh | MP4 H.264 or JPG/PNG; exact res; sRGB; 8–15 s video; ≤50 MB; 30 fps |
| Little screen (indoor) | Pixel res; orientation; loop slot length; ambient context | MP4 H.264 or PNG/JPG; exact res; sRGB; 6–10 s; ≤25 MB; 30 fps |
| Radio station | Frequency (MHz); coverage; spot length (15/30 s); daypart | MP3 or WAV; 44.1 kHz/16-bit min; stereo; −14 LUFS²; exactly 15 or 30 s; ≤10 MB |
| Transit (bus/taxi wrap/car card) | Vehicle type; surface dims cm; substrate; route/fleet size | PDF/X-1a; CMYK; 150 DPI at trim; 1 cm bleed; outlined fonts; ≤150 MB |
| Kiosk (mall/street furniture) | Panel dims cm; backlit y/n; double-sided y/n | PDF/X-1a; CMYK; 200 DPI at trim; 1 cm bleed; outlined fonts; ≤150 MB |

¹ 150 DPI at trim is standard for large-format outdoor viewed from 3 m+; small panels (kiosk)
bump to 200 DPI. ² −14 LUFS aligns with common Mexican broadcast loudness; provider can override.

= Representative end-to-end journeys =
UC-33 — First-time client, single billboard (composes UC-1..UC-4, UC-6): map → detail → new
   campaign → adset → upload validated PDF → checkout → wait approval → live → proof received →
   accept → done.
UC-34 — First-time provider (composes UC-13..UC-17): sign up → list space + declare specs → set
   calendar via URL → first booking → approve → install → upload proof day 2 → payout released.
UC-35 — Disputed proof that travels (composes UC-7, UC-22, UC-25, UC-27): inquiry chat → the same
   chat becomes a confirmed booking chat on approval → client rejects proof for blur → payment
   auto-held (`payments.status=held`) + a `payment_held` flag + THREE chats auto-open (Support↔Client
   / ↔Provider / ↔Payments), each anchored to the held payment+booking (masking relaxes when Support
   joins a client↔provider chat) → Payments+Support review the case across those chats and decide
   (release to provider, or cancel + full refund) — NO automatic re-upload; each chat is one
   chronological history with kind=system transition messages.
UC-36 — Ad creative & installation — WHO does WHAT (actor boundaries; INVARIANT, added to stop the
   recurring "client creates a space/ad" drift):
   - PROVIDER creates the space (billboard, photo/video panel, radio station) with its own
     photos + media-delivery specs. A CLIENT never creates a space, never uploads a space photo,
     and never sets media specs — that is exclusively the provider's job.
   - CLIENT rents spaces from the map; each rented space becomes an ad in the campaign backlog.
     The client's ONLY content action is uploading THEIR creative — the image, video, or audio
     they want shown in that space — for each ad, validated against the space's media-delivery
     specs. The client never mints a space-less ad (see §5 ad-origin invariant).
   - PROVIDER approves the booking and dispatches it to an INSTALLATOR (a subrole employee under
     the provider's own account).
   - INSTALLATOR physically installs the ad and uploads the PROOF of display (photo, or video for
     radio/audio), logged in with their installator subrole under the provider's account. Proofs
     are a provider-side artifact; the client only ACCEPTS or REJECTS a proof, never uploads one.

specs.title: Roadmap, Revisions & Known Gaps
specs.summary: Owner decisions that supersede earlier text (latest wins) and the build phases. Reaffirms decimal-MXN money, account-wide collaborators, client-accepts-proof (B9), the one-chat primitive, and provider Approve/Reject. Team targets ~90% compliance.
specs.body:
These owner decisions SUPERSEDE earlier text where they conflict (latest wins). The team builds
toward ~90% compliance across the design, not 100% — some older text is intentionally stale.

Revised decisions (override above where older):
- MONEY: DECIMAL MXN pesos everywhere (no centavos).
- COLLABORATORS: ACCOUNT-WIDE for BOTH clients and providers; subroles per ecosystem (client:
  publicist/manager; provider: installator/sales/supervisor); under a "Configurations" tab.
- PROOF/PAYMENTS (B9): the CLIENT accepts/rejects the primary proof — acceptance releases payout,
  rejection HOLDS it; Payments doesn't judge content up front (only a read-only view when a
  payment is on hold). Remove Payments proof approve/reject of content.
- CHATS (§10, supersedes the earlier one-object "conversations" note): ONE primitive — a "ticket" is
  just a chat with a Support participant. A chat carries ZERO..MANY attached objects + flags; its
  nature is DERIVED from participants+objects+flags (no `type` column). Admin+Support eagle-eye; only
  SUPPORT entry is announced (relaxes PII), Admin is silent/read-only. The dispute opens THREE chats
  (not a "dual ticket").
- PROVIDER BOOKING ACTION: Approve (and send to an installator) OR Reject (reason optional). Not
  bare Confirm/Cancel.

Roadmap, per-feature build order, and the live code-vs-design gap list are tracked in
`.claude/todos/mvp-sprint.json` (not duplicated here). Shorthand: PHASE 1 = owner-decision fixes +
UI wiring; PHASE 2 = Support edit-any + audit log, Admin eagle-eye; PHASE 3 (deferred) = strikes,
ratings, notifications, escrow/pre-pay, media-spec validator, moderation, invoice line-items.

specs.title: Object Ownership & Access Chain (guardrails)
specs.summary: Authorize by the full ownership chain; 404 not 403; scoped nested bindings; same-account moves only; every ad has a space.
specs.body:
<!-- [2026-08-02] Corrected wip→review per §0: the code landed and OwnershipChainTest is green on
     Postgres, so it is "implemented AND under verification". It clears to `done` only after the
     human walkthrough (create/move/delete adsets+ads; orphans survive; nothing answers 403). -->


[owner 2026-08-01] APPROVED. Every screen and endpoint authorizes by the OWNERSHIP CHAIN, never by
the parent alone. (UC-43.)

**The chain:** `user → account → campaign → adset → ad`; a `space` hangs off the PROVIDER's account.
Access requires the WHOLE chain to belong to the caller's account, plus the caller's role/subrole.

**Rules:**
1. Nested route bindings are ALWAYS scoped (`->scopeBindings()`) PLUS an explicit
   `abort_unless($child->parent_id === $parent->id, 404)` in each method. Verifying only the parent
   (e.g. "the campaign is mine") is NOT enough — that was the IDOR found on
   `/client/campaigns/{c}/adsets/{a}` and `/ads/{ad}`.
2. **404, never 403**, for an object outside the caller's account — a 403 confirms the object exists
   and leaks its existence.
3. **Moves** (see the table) are allowed WITHIN one account, across campaigns and adsets; they are
   forbidden across accounts. A move carries its dependents: moving a booked ad updates
   `bookings.adset_id` (and `campaign_id`) in the SAME transaction.
4. **INVARIANT — every ad has a `space_id`.** A space-less ad has nobody to pay and nowhere to send
   the files, so it can never be booked. Any UI that mints one is a bug (see §5, ad origin): the
   "type a name + pick a media type + upload" form must NOT exist — ads come from booking a space or
   from moving one in from the backlog.
5. `account_grants` (per-account RBAC overlay) is evaluated AFTER the global role matrix; grants never
   leak across accounts. (Later task.)

**Move matrix:**
| Move | Allowed | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|
| ad → another adset, SAME campaign | YES | same `account_id` |
| ad → adset of ANOTHER campaign, same account | YES | same `account_id` |
| ad → backlog (becomes orphan) | YES | same `account_id` |
| adset → another campaign, same account | YES | same `account_id` |
| ad / adset → anything of ANOTHER account | NO — 404 | different account |

**Adset deletion** — an adset is only a GROUPING label, so deleting it must NOT destroy ads:
`ads.adset_id` migrates from `cascadeOnDelete` to **`nullOnDelete`**. On delete the client is asked
where the ads go: MOVE them to another adset, or LEAVE them orphaned. Orphaned ≠ stopped — anything
already paid keeps running; an orphan is just harder to find for further actions (an unpaid one
simply never ran, like an abandoned shopping cart).

specs.title: Landing publica y alta desde fuera
specs.summary: Una pagina publica que explica el marketplace y da de alta. Vive en `landing/`, es una aplicacion Angular aparte, y su formulario entra por el mismo `POST /api/register` que usa el producto.
specs.body:
ALCANCE (owner 2026-08-05). Cuatro rutas y ni una mas: la pagina, `/terminos`, `/privacidad` y `/gracias`. Todo lo demas es una seccion anclada dentro de la misma pagina, no una ruta.

POR QUE UNA APLICACION APARTE Y NO UNA RUTA DE `frontend/`. La landing la carga gente que no ha iniciado sesion y que decide en segundos: no debe arrastrar el bundle del producto, ni su router protegido, ni sus interceptores de token. Sale en 74 kB comprimidos frente a los cientos del panel. Ademas se despliega en sitios distintos —la landing a un CDN, el producto detras del login— y mezclarlas obliga a desplegar las dos cada vez que cambia una coma del titular.

DONDE VAN LOS DATOS DEL FORMULARIO (decidido 2026-08-05, owner). A `POST /api/register`, el endpoint publico que ya existe. Se descartaron las otras dos opciones y conviene que conste por que: un endpoint nuevo de leads habria anadido tabla, migracion y entrada en `endpoints[]` para algo que quiza se sustituya por un formulario externo; y un formulario sin destino habria sido EH-8 literal, un control que solo existe para aparentar. Al ir contra el alta real, la landing hereda tambien el spam que reciba — es el coste asumido de que el embudo funcione desde el primer dia.

UN SOLO PUNTO DE INTEGRACION. Todo lo que sabe DONDE se mandan los datos vive en `landing/src/app/shared/signup.service.ts`. El owner avisa de que probablemente cambie el formulario mas adelante, asi que cambiarlo tiene que ser reescribir un fichero y no perseguir llamadas por las secciones.

LA LANDING NO GUARDA SESION. El alta devuelve un token y la landing lo ignora a proposito: es captacion, no producto. Quien se registra pasa por el acuse y entra por la puerta normal. Guardarlo obligaria a la landing a tener politica de tokens, y esa es superficie de autenticacion en una pagina publica y cacheada.

TEXTOS LEGALES. Terminos y privacidad estan escritos y describen lo que la plataforma hace HOY (retencion del pago, disputas, colaboradores que no se desvinculan, nada en uso se destruye). NO los ha revisado nadie con formacion legal, y eso esta escrito en la propia pagina y en LAND-1. Es requisito de apertura al publico, no de cierre de la spec.

ESTILO. Familia Be Agency / Bridge / Impreza: secciones a sangre completa alternando fondo, titular muy grande con una palabra en cursiva y acento, filas de iconos, cifras, testimonio y cierre. Los tres temas de referencia estaban inaccesibles desde el entorno de trabajo (HTTP 000 en los tres), asi que se reprodujo la familia sin copiar HTML ajeno.

userStories.title: Client searches & multi-selects spaces on the map
userStories.detail: Client lands on a map centered on their geolocation (default Monterrey). The nearest-first right rail lists nearby spaces sorted near-to-far, tagged by type (billboard, big/little screen, radio, kiosk, transit). The list is multi-select; selecting shows 'Add to an existing campaign' / 'Add to a new campaign' (new campaign fires a 10-second 'Go to my new campaign' toast). Radio 'in range' means inside the current map view.

userStories.title: Client organizes campaign / adset / ads from the backlog
userStories.detail: Selected spaces sit in the campaign backlog as orphan ads until placed. The campaign view's Orphan-spaces list has a one-click 'Move all to new adset'; orphans can't reach checkout. Adsets are pure grouping labels; the way to populate an adset is to move ads in from the backlog — never mint a new space-less ad.

userStories.title: Client uploads spec-validated creative
userStories.detail: The client's only content action is uploading THEIR creative (image/video/audio) for each ad, validated against the space's media-delivery specs. The upload control shows the provider's upload-instructions inline; on spec-mismatch the upload is rejected with a clear message (e.g. 'your file must be PDF/X-1a, CMYK, 150 DPI at trim, 1 cm bleed'). One file per ad (MVP).

userStories.title: Client checks out & pays (ONE invoice per campaign)
userStories.detail: One checkout per campaign covers all ads regardless of provider, producing ONE invoice with per-ad line items and per-provider payouts. Refund policy, terms & conditions, and privacy policy are linked on the checkout screen before paying. The gateway processing fee is added on top (paid gross by the client). An orphan ad cannot be checked out / go live.

userStories.title: Client books-for-later / pre-pays into escrow (AFTER-MVP)
userStories.detail: When a window isn't free, the client can 'book it for later' via a per-space queue: PRE-PAY (funds captured into escrow, joins the provider's waiting list) or NON-PRE-PAY (queued FCFS). Confirming pre-pay is not final approval and locks in neither party; on any cancel/reject escrowed funds return to the wallet. If the slot never opens within the expiry window, the client is refunded.

userStories.title: Client reviews & ACCEPTS proof -> payout releasable
userStories.detail: The client (or a collaborator per role) reviews the provider's primary proof. Accepting sets proofs.status=client_accepted, making the payment releasable so Payments can MANUALLY release the payout. Payments never reviews proof content.

userStories.title: Client REJECTS proof / flags mismatch -> dispute (3 chats + hold)
userStories.detail: If the client rejects the proof (or a collaborator flags a mismatch), the only automatic actions are: payout is AUTO-HELD (payments.status=held); a payment_held flag with reason text is attached; and THREE Support-anchored chats auto-open (Support<->Client, Support<->Provider, Support<->Payments), each anchored to the held payment+booking. There is NO automatic re-upload window — any request for a corrected proof is a human Support action.

userStories.title: Client opens a provider inquiry from the provider's published listing
userStories.detail: A client reaches a provider ONLY from a listing the provider published (space/ad), which opens a client_provider chat with the space attached as context. Providers have no public profile/UI, so this is the ONLY path to a provider. An inquiry chat becomes a confirmed booking chat only when both provider approval and client payment complete. PII masking applies until Support joins.

userStories.title: Client contacts Support from Messages or an ad/adset/campaign object
userStories.detail: From the Messages tab or an ad/adset/campaign object the counterparty is Support (support_client); the object rides along as context and does NOT pull in the provider. A Billing-opened chat is Support-fronted with the payment/invoice attached, and Payments is looped in via the internal Support<->Payments chat — Payments never faces the client directly. 'Contact support' is simply 'open a chat'.

userStories.title: Client cancels a booking (refund per policy)
userStories.detail: Cancellation refunds are 100% by default UNLESS the booking was already in process (install work started), then reduced to cover work performed (stated in the T&C). Free pre-approval cancel; nothing post-display unless a proof fails; full refund on proof-miss auto-cancel or provider cancel. Payments executes the refund to the wallet.

userStories.title: Client views wallet & withdraws
userStories.detail: The wallet is an append-only, double-entry ledger; balance = SUM(amount), never a writable column. GET /wallet returns balance + entries. Withdraw (POST /client/wallet/withdraw) is BLOCKED while any dispute/hold is open. Every refund/payout carries an idempotency key so a retry can't double-pay.

userStories.title: Client rates a provider (AFTER-MVP)
userStories.detail: Only clients rate, only after a campaign with that provider ended OR ran live >=30 days, one per client per campaign (POST /client/campaigns/{c}/rating). A provider's star rating (1-5 + count) on each space = average of per-campaign ratings + optional comment. Ratings are immutable and fully transparent — no client edit/delete.

userStories.title: Provider lists a space & declares specs
userStories.detail: The provider creates the space (with photos, pricing per day/month/custom, physical + media-delivery specs, availability calendar). Media specs auto-populate from a per-type template (provider can tighten) plus free-text rules. A client never creates a space or sets media specs — that is exclusively the provider's job.

userStories.title: Provider manages availability calendar (iCal sync)
userStories.detail: The availability UI strongly recommends connecting a live calendar URL (.ical or public Google/Outlook); a '?' help button explains how to find it. The staleness clock is measured from the last successful sync or last manual edit — never from space creation; older than 7d fires an alert next to that space. An offline imported calendar falls back to its last-known range rather than vanishing.

userStories.title: Provider approves / rejects a booking request
userStories.detail: The provider acts with Approve or Reject only — NO counter-offers; the rejection reason is optional (stored, helps re-submit). The request queue shows client, dates, total, and the attached media file. Go-live is PER-AD: each ad is approved, goes live, and bills on its own approval independently. Confirmed bookings move to an installation queue for Installator collaborators.

userStories.title: Provider / Installator uploads the PRIMARY proof
userStories.detail: Only the PRIMARY proof makes a booking eligible for payout. Within the deadline it is uploaded by the provider owner OR the provider's Installator or Supervisor subrole — NOT Sales, and no client-side role. It is a photo (printed/screen) or short video (radio/audio). Proofs are a provider-side artifact; the client only accepts or rejects.

userStories.title: Provider receives a payout
userStories.detail: Payouts happen ASAP but must be APPROVED by Payments first (Support flags only). Once approved and nothing holds it, the payout enters the processing queue (grace window, default 1h, reversible) then dispatches to the provider's Mercado Pago/PayPal. Admin has a 24h window to stop it. Payouts are PER-PROVIDER even within one multi-provider campaign invoice.

userStories.title: Provider views strike counter / appeals a strike
userStories.detail: Strikes accrue on missed proof deadline, provider cancel of a confirmed booking, or upheld mismatch; the trailing-90-day count shows on the provider dashboard. 3 strikes in 90 days flags the account for Admin review (possible freeze). The provider appeals via a support chat; SUPPORT (not Payments) can remove a strike (reversible, audited).

userStories.title: Owner invites & manages collaborators
userStories.detail: The account owner invites collaborators by email from an account-scoped Collaborators screen under the Configurations tab. Collaborators are ACCOUNT-scoped (point to account_id, unique(account_id,email)) and, per subrole, see/act across ALL of that account's campaigns/spaces. The owner can see any conversation a collaborator has.

userStories.title: Collaborator acts within subrole scope
userStories.detail: A collaborator acts only within its subrole scope, enforced by the per-account account_grants overlay evaluated after the global matrix. CLIENT side: Publicist (operational, no money) / Manager (everything incl. money). PROVIDER side: Installator (proof-upload only) / Sales (chat replies only) / Supervisor (edit almost everything except owner-only powers and money).

userStories.title: Support joins a client<->provider chat (announced, PII relax)
userStories.detail: Any support agent can pick up a chat with a Support participant (the queue is DERIVED). A Support join into a client<->provider chat is ANNOUNCED (a system message) and RELAXES PII masking for that chat. Support sets the chat to in_progress on pickup.

userStories.title: Support investigates a dispute & RAISES a money flag
userStories.detail: Support investigates across the dispute chats and RAISES money flags (refund/payout_hold/payment_held) via POST /chats/{c}/flags — but Support only FLAGS, it never executes money. A flag annotates the WHY; the authoritative money state stays on payments.status. Support leans toward the client and watches for fraud.

userStories.title: Support edits a non-money object (audited)
userStories.detail: Support can edit every NON-money object (spaces, ads, users, bookings, collaborators) via PUT /support/{resource}/{id} (PLANNED) — every action is audit-logged. Support has NO money-execution power.

userStories.title: Support reverses a strike (audited)
userStories.detail: SUPPORT (not Payments) can remove a strike from the counter — reversible and audited — typically after a provider appeal via a support chat. Strike accrual/removal routes Support then Admin, never Payments.

userStories.title: Payments approves/executes payment & payout (processing queue)
userStories.detail: Payments is the ONLY role that moves money: approves/rejects payments and executes payouts. Releasing a payout enters the processing queue (payments.status=processing) for a reversible grace window before dispatch; during it Payments or Support can pull it back to held with no gateway call. Once the gateway reports settled the payout is TERMINAL and holdPayout is a NO-OP.

userStories.title: Payments executes a refund
userStories.detail: Payments executes ALL refunds (mocked); Support only flags. Refunds go to the client's wallet with a unique idempotency key (no double-pay), enforcing SUM(refunds) <= captured. Cancellation refunds are 100% by default unless the booking was in process.

userStories.title: Payments huddles with Support in the internal chat
userStories.detail: When a client rejects proof, a Support<->Payments internal chat auto-opens anchored to the held payment+booking (payment_held flag) — the ONLY chat Payments is in on that dispute. Payments never faces the client directly; it coordinates the money decision (release or cancel+refund) with Support there. The client never sees this membership-ACL'd chat; Admin observes read-only.

userStories.title: Admin chat oversight (read-only, incognito)
userStories.detail: Admin reads EVERY chat (including closed ones, full unmasked history) via ONE read-only/incognito screen GET /admin/oversight/chats with filters (nature/flag/object/status/participant). Admin never posts as a ghost; its only chat write-power is reopening a closed chat for investigation. This replaces the former conversations + tickets oversight views.

userStories.title: Admin moderation: takedown / restore / freeze
userStories.detail: Three levels of taking a listing/provider off: Pause/unpublish (provider's own, reversible); Takedown/restore (admin moderation, POST /admin/spaces/{s}/takedown|restore, provider cannot self-reverse); Freeze (account-level, POST /admin/providers/{u}/freeze|unfreeze — pauses new bookings AND auto-cancels upcoming ones with full refunds, busts permission/session cache and revokes tokens immediately).

userStories.title: Admin configures System Configurations + RBAC matrix
userStories.detail: Admin tunes System Configurations (GET,PUT /admin/configurations): proof deadline, strike window/threshold, pre-pay expiry, calendar staleness, payout-stop window, payout processing grace, cancellation refund policy, currency/timezone, auto-approve threshold, rate limits, audit retention. Changing a value offers 'apply to in-flight' vs 'new only' (config snapshotted onto each booking). Admin also edits the global role_permissions matrix (cannot lock out admin).

userStories.title: Admin reviews the immutable audit log
userStories.detail: The append-only audit log records one entry per action of ANY role with actor, target, before/after, timestamp; queryable as per-object history via GET /admin/audit (?target_type, ?target_id). Admin is read-only. AFTER-MVP: DB-level immutability (INSERT-only + trigger, optional hash-chain).

userStories.title: Admin payout-stop window & clawback decision
userStories.detail: Once Payments approves a payout, Admin has a configurable window (default 24h) to stop it; if Admin doesn't, funds release automatically. Clawback: if a refunded client is later suspended for fraud, the platform freezes the wallet and alerts Payments — Payments cannot pull funds; the frozen balance waits for an Admin decision (claw back via negative ledger entry / keep frozen / release).

userStories.title: Journey: first-time client, single billboard
userStories.detail: Composes UC-1..UC-4, UC-6: map -> detail -> new campaign -> adset -> upload validated PDF -> checkout -> wait approval -> live -> proof received -> accept -> done.

userStories.title: Journey: first-time provider
userStories.detail: Composes UC-13..UC-17: sign up -> list space + declare specs -> set calendar via URL -> first booking -> approve -> install -> upload proof day 2 -> payout released.

userStories.title: Journey: disputed proof that travels
userStories.detail: Composes UC-7, UC-22, UC-25, UC-27: inquiry chat -> the same chat becomes a confirmed booking chat on approval -> client rejects proof for blur -> payment auto-held (payments.status=held) + a payment_held flag + THREE chats auto-open (Support<->Client / ->Provider / ->Payments), each anchored to the held payment+booking (masking relaxes when Support joins a client<->provider chat) -> Payments+Support review the case and decide (release, or cancel + full refund) — NO automatic re-upload; each chat is one chronological history with kind=system transition messages.

userStories.title: Journey: ad creative & installation actor boundaries
userStories.detail: INVARIANT actor boundaries: PROVIDER creates the space (+ photos + media specs); a CLIENT never creates a space or sets media specs. CLIENT rents spaces from the map (each becomes a backlog ad) and only uploads THEIR creative, validated against the space's specs — never mints a space-less ad. PROVIDER approves the booking and dispatches to an INSTALLATOR. INSTALLATOR physically installs and uploads the PROOF; the client only accepts or rejects a proof.

userStories.title: Admin deletion guardrails / 'programmed for deletion'
userStories.detail: A hard delete of any object (users, campaigns, adsets, ads, spaces) is BLOCKED whenever it has open support chats, a booking in progress, or unsettled funds. Instead deletion is a 'programmed for deletion' state: the object is unpublished, stops new activity, and stays visible with the legend until current bookings finish, then is removed.

userStories.title: Notifications & alert-schema dispatch
userStories.detail: Domain events (BookingApproved, ProofRejected, ...) fan out through queued listeners via a channel/urgency lookup — no scattered Notification::send. The ~35-event alert schema (in-app/email/SMS-mock, urgency low..critical) is tabulated in §19; SMS is reserved for Payments alerts and cancellations.

userStories.title: Provider self-pause / unpublish a space (reversible)
userStories.detail: A provider can pause/unpublish their own listing, hiding it and stopping new bookings while paused; it is reversible by the provider (unlike an admin takedown, which the provider cannot self-reverse).

userStories.title: Proof-deadline cron: day-3/4 reminders -> day-5 auto-cancel
userStories.detail: The proof-deadline cron (AFTER-MVP) fires reminders on day 3 and day 4 (day-4 includes SMS), then on missing the day-5 deadline auto-cancels the booking, refunds the client to wallet in full, and accrues a provider strike. The cron locks the booking and re-checks proof IS NULL inside the transaction.

userStories.title: User signs in and the platform grants exactly their role's capabilities
userStories.detail: A registered user — client, provider, support, payments, admin, or a collaborator with a subrole — authenticates with their credentials and lands in a workspace scoped to their role. Navigation, actions, and visible data are shaped by the RBAC matrix: a client never sees the admin panel, an installator never sees money flags. Every user gets a coherent, uncluttered experience that exposes only what they are allowed to do. A failed login returns a clear, non-leaky error; a valid session persists until logout.

userStories.title: User resolves everything in one seamless conversation — no juggling tickets vs chat
userStories.detail: When a user needs help they open a single conversation from the Support button (or from an ad/adset/campaign object, or a payment) and just type. Behind one uniform chat UI, Support — and Payments when money is involved — join the same thread; the user never files a 'ticket', never learns a second tool, never repeats context. Attachments, history, and the object in question travel with the conversation, so resolving an issue feels like messaging, not paperwork.

userStories.title: Every screen and endpoint authorizes by the ownership chain
userStories.detail: Access is granted only when the WHOLE chain belongs to the caller's account: user -> account -> campaign -> adset -> ad (a space hangs off the provider's account), plus the caller's role/subrole. Checking the parent alone is not enough - that is the IDOR where a client could open /client/campaigns/1/adsets/99 and read, rename or delete another account's adset. A break anywhere in the chain returns 404, never 403, so the existence of a foreign object is never leaked. Moves are allowed within one account across campaigns and adsets and carry their dependents (a booked ad's booking follows it); cross-account moves are refused. Every ad must have a space_id - a space-less ad has nobody to pay and nowhere to send files.

userStories.title: Una disputa abierta detiene la mano de Payments
userStories.detail: El cliente rechaza la prueba y la plataforma congela el dinero: se abren tres hilos y el pago queda retenido. Cuando alguien de Payments abre ese pago en su bandeja y pulsa aprobar, la plataforma no lo deja pasar: responde 409, nombra la disputa y no mueve un peso. Tampoco escribe una linea de auditoria, porque un registro de algo que no ocurrio se lee despues como si hubiera ocurrido. Para cobrar hay que cerrar la disputa primero, y ese orden no se negocia: de lo contrario los tres hilos seguirian diciendo "pago retenido" mientras la columna que manda diria lo contrario, y nadie sabria cual de las dos creer.

userStories.title: El observador invisible deja huella
userStories.detail: El admin entra a cualquier hilo sin que los participantes se enteren: no figura como participante, no escribe, no se anuncia. Ese silencio es deliberado y es justo por eso que la plataforma anota cada vez que abre un hilo concreto, con quien fue y a que hora. Listar la cola no deja huella — auditar cada refresco enterraria la linea que importa bajo ruido. Lo que se registra es la lectura de un hilo, que es donde el admin ve el telefono sin enmascarar de un cliente y la conversacion interna sobre su dinero.

userStories.title: Todo veredicto lleva nombre y hora
userStories.detail: Cuando el cliente acepta o rechaza una prueba, la plataforma guarda quien la reviso y cuando, no solo el resultado. Semanas despues, si esa reserva termina en disputa, Support abre el caso y puede decir "la acepto esta persona, este dia" en lugar de mirar una fila sin firma y tener que reconstruirlo desde los mensajes.

userStories.title: Nadie se va llevandose el trabajo de los demas
userStories.detail: Un usuario del que dependen campanas, espacios, reservas o saldo no se puede borrar, y la negativa no vive en la interfaz sino en la base de datos, que es donde no se olvida. Antes bastaba una instruccion para que una cuenta arrastrara en cascada todo lo que colgaba de ella; el registro de auditoria anotaba fielmente una perdida que ya no podia deshacer. El admin puede apartar a una persona de sus roles; borrar la cuenta es cosa del dueno, y solo cuando ya nada depende de ella.
userStories.satisfiedBy: FK restrictOnDelete + Admin\UserController sin destroy + migracion revoke_users_delete_permission

userStories.title: Una persona, una invitacion por cuenta
userStories.detail: El dueno invita a un colaborador por correo desde su propia pestana de Colaboradores, que vive en la cuenta y no dentro de una campana. Si esa persona ya fue invitada, la plataforma lo dice en vez de crear un segundo registro. Antes la restriccion contaba por campana, asi que la misma persona acumulaba una invitacion por cada campana y la restriccion no restringia lo que aparentaba.

userStories.title: Cada subrol ve exactamente su parcela
userStories.detail: Del lado del cliente hay dos personajes: el publicist, que opera sin tocar dinero, y el manager, que puede todo incluido el dinero. Del lado del proveedor hay tres: el installator, que ve las peticiones de espacios nuevos y sube pruebas y NO entra a los chats; el sales, que responde mensajes; y el supervisor, que hace todo salvo quitar gente, tocar configuracion o borrar un espacio. Por eso el formulario del cliente ofrece solo publicist y manager. Antes aceptaba installator: el registro se creaba, la persona veia campanas, y despues no podia abrir un solo hilo sin que nada le explicara por que.

userStories.title: La matriz de permisos no se puede cerrar sobre si misma
userStories.detail: El admin reescribe quien hace que, pero hay dos cosas que la matriz no le deja hacer: quitarse la gestion de usuarios, y concederle a nadie —ni a si mismo— el borrado de cuentas. Apartar a alguien de sus roles es la unica via sancionada para sacarlo, de modo que perder esa capacidad lo dejaria sin herramienta y sin aviso. El intento de reescribir la matriz OMITIENDO la clave de usuarios se rechaza igual, porque es el mismo encierro entrando por otra puerta.

userStories.title: Ningun ajuste visible es decorativo
userStories.detail: Todo lo que aparece en la pantalla de Configuracion cambia algo real, y las claves que ya no lee nadie se retiran en vez de quedarse por si acaso. Habia un dial de "ventana de re-subida: 48 horas", editable y visible, sobre una regla retirada meses antes: ningun codigo lo consultaba. Un ajuste que miente es peor que uno que falta, porque el admin se va convencido de haber cambiado algo.

userStories.title: El dinero listo y el dinero congelado nunca se parecen
userStories.detail: Payments abre su bandeja y ve dos cosas distintas: lo que esta libre para pagar porque el cliente acepto la prueba, y lo que esta congelado dentro de una disputa. Antes ambos decian "held" y el tablero los sumaba en la misma tarjeta, de modo que la pantalla no distinguia lo que se debe pagar de lo que no se debe tocar. Ademas la orden de liberar consulta el estado del propio pago: antes volvia a leer las pruebas de la reserva, asi que en una reserva con varias pruebas bastaba una aceptada para habilitar el pago aunque otra siguiera en disputa.

userStories.title: Un colaborador solo alcanza los hilos de la cuenta que lo invito
userStories.detail: Un proveedor invita a alguien como sales o supervisor y esa persona entra a los hilos de SU cuenta. A los de otro proveedor, no. Parece obvio y no lo era: mientras no existio la tabla de cuentas, la comprobacion solo podia preguntar "¿esta persona tiene un permiso de sales o supervisor en algun sitio?", sin un ambito contra el que medirlo. Bastaba un permiso en un proveedor para abrir los hilos de TODOS los proveedores. El lado del cliente ya estaba acotado; el del proveedor no tenia con que acotarse. Ahora los dos preguntan por la misma cuenta.

userStories.title: Un anuncio retirado por moderacion no lo devuelve su dueno
userStories.detail: El admin retira un anuncio y escribe por que. El proveedor sigue pudiendo pausar y despausar lo suyo — eso nunca se le quita — pero despausar no levanta un takedown: la plataforma responde 409 y el anuncio sigue fuera del catalogo. Son tres niveles distintos y el orden importa: la pausa es del proveedor, el takedown es del admin, y el freeze es de la cuenta entera. Restaurar tampoco deshace la pausa que el proveedor haya puesto por su cuenta: cada palanca vuelve solo lo que ella misma hizo.

userStories.title: Recuperar un pago ya entregado se llama por su nombre
userStories.detail: Cuando el cliente acepta la prueba se sella la hora en que el pago quedo liberable, y desde ahi corre una ventana configurable en la que el admin todavia puede detenerlo. Pasada la ventana, si el dinero ya salio, recuperarlo no es un reembolso: es un clawback, y la plataforma lo escribe como un asiento NEGATIVO propio en el libro. Nunca lo compensa contra el asiento de salida, porque un libro donde dos hechos se cancelan entre si ya no cuenta lo que paso — solo el saldo. El pago vuelve a `held`, que es la verdad: el proveedor ya no tiene ese dinero.

userStories.title: Borrar un espacio en uso no lo borra: lo despublica y lo agenda
userStories.detail: El proveedor pide borrar un espacio. Si todavia hay clientes contando con el — reservas vivas o dinero sin liquidar — la plataforma se niega y le dice CUALES son, porque un "no" sin motivo lo deja adivinando a cual de sus clientes le esta estorbando. Si no hay nada colgando, el espacio sale del catalogo como `unpublished` y queda con fecha; nada se destruye en ese momento. Despausar no lo rescata: la pausa es la palanca del proveedor y el borrado programado es otra cosa, asi que hace falta cancelarlo a proposito. La destruccion la ejecuta una persona con un comando, y ese comando vuelve a revisar los bloqueos antes de tocar nada — entre que se agendo y hoy pudieron pasar semanas, y alguien pudo volver a reservar.

userStories.title: Alguien que no conoce la plataforma llega, entiende que es y se da de alta
userStories.story: Como persona que llega por primera vez, quiero entender en una pantalla que es este sitio y de que lado estoy —busco espacio o lo tengo—, para poder crear una cuenta sin hablar con nadie ni pedir un presupuesto por correo.
acceptance: La pagina explica el marketplace sin pedir registro para leerla.
El formulario pregunta de que lado viene, porque `users.role` decide el menu entero desde el primer login y equivocarse ahi obliga a rehacer el alta.
Al enviarlo se crea la cuenta de verdad contra `POST /api/register` y se navega al acuse.
Un email ya registrado responde con un mensaje que lo dice por su nombre, no con un error generico.
Terminos y privacidad son alcanzables desde el propio formulario antes de aceptarlos.

remaining: DEV-signing-01 [P3 infra, not MVP] Commits land on GitHub as 'Unverified'. NOT an authorship problem: author AND committer are already noreply@anthropic.com. The only missing piece is the SIGNATURE, and it cannot be produced where the commits are made — in Claude Code (web) the container has commit.gpgsign=true pointing at /home/claude/.ssh/commit_signing_key.pub, which is 0 BYTES, has no matching private key, and ssh-keygen is not even installed. So the stop-hook's 'git commit --amend --reset-author' remedy is a no-op there (and destructive when the commit carries the owner's authorship — it already nearly wiped ec0317c). A signature also does NOT survive patch transport: a .patch carries author/date/message/diff, never the signature, so the commit that matters is the one CREATED IN THE CODESPACE. FIX, one-time in the Codespace: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'marcomarkkez@gmail.com' -f ~/.ssh/git_signing -N '' ; git config --global gpg.format ssh ; git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/git_signing.pub ; git config --global commit.gpgsign true ; then paste ~/.ssh/git_signing.pub into GitHub > Settings > SSH and GPG keys > New SSH key with key type SIGNING KEY (uploading it as an Authentication key is the classic mistake — GitHub will not use it to verify and everything still shows Unverified). CAVEAT: ~/.ssh does not survive a Codespace rebuild — to persist it, put the key in a dotfiles repo or a Codespace secret. The stop hook will KEEP firing in every web session regardless; that is the container image's empty key, not something fixable from inside the session.

git push: RESOLVED for the Codespace (p64–p67 pushed fine from there). It stays blocked from Claude Code (web) sessions — token scope, not repo visibility — which is why delivery is patch-only; see claude.md Learnings.
